sections.title: How it works
sections.content: You know *elkészített* from B1 Unit 2 (*az elkészített étel*): the third-person past form in *-t/-tt* can stand before a noun and describe it by what was done to it. In a history it packs an earlier event into the noun phrase: *a kivégzett miniszterelnök*, *az áthelyezett szobor*. The participle stands before the noun and takes no ending; only the noun takes case endings: *a kivégzett miniszterelnököt*. New in this lesson is the vocabulary of 1956.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: The executed prime minister was reburied in 1989.
Az áthelyezett szobor új helye a Jászai Mari tér lett.
The relocated statue's new place became Jászai Mari tér.
A felavatott emlékművet a bírálók vitatták.
The critics disputed the memorial that had been unveiled.
